title: Confidence Lift Ledger and Launch Health Kit
content:
Purpose and scope:
This working doc captures the "Confidence Lift" ledger — a compact scorecard that synthesizes product, performance, and economic signals into a single launch confidence view. Use this during feature go/no-go reviews and during staggered rollouts to decide traffic ramps and fallback thresholds.

Intended audience:
- Product Ops leads running release committees
- Product managers owning launches
- SRE/Observability reps for metric gating
- Solutions/SE for customer readiness signals

High-level approach (quick):
1) Surface 8–10 high-value KPIs across quality, performance, economics, and adoption that matter for this feature.
2) Normalize each KPI into a 0–100 band (simple min/max mapping) so we can average with optional weighting.
3) Compute Confidence Lift = weighted average of KPI bands.
4) Define explicit thresholds and mitigations for each band below the gate.

Core KPI set (suggested for LLM-powered product launches):
- User-facing quality (QA): sample-eval pass rate vs. golden prompts (goal >= 90%)
- Regression delta: percent of critical regressions vs baseline (goal <= 2%)
- Latency (P95 request-to-first-byte; goal <= 350ms hosted, <= 200ms dedicated)
- Cost per active session (USD) normalized by expected volume (goal reduces baseline by >= 5%)
- Error rate (server errors + model fallback rate; goal <= 0.5%)
- Availability (successful request rate; goal >= 99.9%)
- Conversion uplift (feature-specific business metric; e.g., CTA rate increase)
- Operational cost volatility (week-over-week variance of spend; goal <= 10%)

Example KPI weighting (editable):
- Quality (QA sample pass): weight 30
- Latency (P95): weight 20
- Error rate + availability combined: weight 20
- Cost per session: weight 15
- Conversion uplift: weight 10
- Volatility: weight 5

Normalization notes (quick formulas to implement in a sheet):
- For metrics where lower is better (latency, error rate, cost): normalized = 100 * (max_threshold - value) / (max_threshold - min_threshold)
- For metrics where higher is better (availability, QA pass): normalized = 100 * (value - min_threshold) / (max_threshold - min_threshold)
- Clamp normalized to 0..100.
- Example thresholds (editable per launch): latency min=100ms, max=1000ms; QA pass min=50%, max=95%

Confidence Lift calculation (textual):
- For each KPI: compute normalized_kpi in 0..100.
- Weighted sum: sum(normalized_kpi * weight) / sum(weights).
- Confidence bands: 
  - Green: >= 80
  - Amber: 60–79
  - Red: < 60

Quick-run checklist (pre-launch, gate items):
- [ ] Sample-eval set created and run (owner: PM)
- [ ] QA pass rate >= target on baseline and canary (owner: QA lead)
- [ ] Load tests executed for expected QPS with matching sequence length distribution (owner: SRE)
- [ ] Cost simulation performed (owner: FinOps)
- [ ] Observability: dashboards wired, token-level cost breakdown, trace hooks (owner: Observability lead)
- [ ] Rollout policy configured (canary %, escalation windows, fallback model) (owner: Product Ops)
- [ ] Support & CS playbook drafted for top-10 customer issues (owner: CS lead)
- [ ] Legal/compliance signoff for sensitive data paths (owner: Security)

Launch gating matrix (operational mapping):
- Gate: Confidence Lift green + no critical regressions -> proceed to canary (10–20% traffic)
- Gate: Amber -> proceed to restricted canary (5–10%) with rapid-check window; require mitigation plan and SRE on-call
- Gate: Red -> hold launch; require root-cause + corrective release

Runbook snippets for gated amber conditions (practical):
- If P95 spikes 2x baseline during canary: reduce traffic to previous stable model + open incident (SRE)
- If cost per session > 20% over projection for three consecutive hours: pause traffic ramp and notify FinOps + PM
- If QA pass drops below threshold on new prompt set: rollback model variant and kick off eval triage (PM + Applied ML)

Operational template to paste into a sheet (columns to capture each day of rollout):
- date, traffic_pct, conf_lift_score, conf_band, p95_latency_ms, error_rate_pct, qa_pass_pct, cost_per_session_usd, conv_uplift_pct, notes, owner_action

Sample synthetic ledger rows (notes-to-self style):
- 2026-01-12 | 5% | 86 | green | 180ms | 0.2% | 92% | $0.072 | +4.2% | stable, slight regressions in edge cases | Elena investigating prompt parsing
- 2026-01-13 | 15% | 74 | amber | 410ms | 0.6% | 88% | $0.095 | +6.8% | latency under load; reduce batch size on dedicated pool | SRE actioned

Open questions / assumptions (capture early):
- Are we comfortable using conversion uplift from a 2-week A/B as the business KPI for early rollouts?
- Which sequence length distribution should we use for cost sim — conservative or expected 95th percentile?
- Is there an explicit SLA delta that triggers enterprise customer notification?

Back-of-envelope cost velocity check (how to think about it):
- If expected sessions/day = 50k, and cost_per_session target = $0.05, weekly spend ~ $175k. A 10% overspend is $17.5k — decide threshold for automated hold.

Escalation contacts (quick):
- Product Ops: Priya Nair (on-call rota)
- SRE: Marco Ruiz (pager)
- Observability: Jonah Blake
- FinOps: Elena Park

Decisions taken in this doc (history):
- 2025-12-03: Agreed default weighting (prod ops meeting)
- 2026-01-08: Added volatility KPI -> requested by FinOps

Immediate next steps before next review:
- PMs to supply feature-specific conversion baseline and golden eval prompts by 2026-02-15
- SRE to attach load-test matrix + sample JMeter config (ENG-4827)
- Observability to create a conf_lift dashboard template in Grafana and share link

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally light-weight and extensible. The goal is a single-pane confidence signal for rapid decisions. Add/remove KPIs per feature, but keep the normalization approach consistent so scores remain comparable across launches.
- Prefer pragmatic thresholds over perfect calibration in early rollouts; refine weighting after 3 launches.

-- end of working doc --
